definitions.gloss: helpless; can't be helped; nothing can be done
definitions.explanation: Expressing that a situation is beyond one's control and there is no way to fix or change it.
Describing a person or thing as beyond improvement or redemption.

examples.japanese: こればかりはどうしようもない。
examples.english: There's nothing that can be done about this.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ったらどうしようもない。{中止|ちゅうし}にするしかない。
examples.english: If it rains, there's nothing we can do. We'll have to cancel.

examples.japanese: どうしようもない{寂|さび}しさを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt an overwhelming sense of loneliness.

examples.japanese: あいつは{本当|ほんとう}にどうしようもないやつだ。
{何度|なんど}{注意|ちゅうい}しても{直|なお}らない。どうしようもない。
examples.english: No matter how many times I warn him, he doesn't change. He's hopeless.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}はどうしようもない{不良|ふりょう}だったが、{今|いま}は{立派|りっぱ}な{社会人|しゃかいじん}だ。
examples.english: He was a hopeless delinquent when he was young, but now he's a fine member of society.

notes: Composed of どう (how) + しよう (volitional of する) + もない (not even). Literally means "there isn't even a way to do anything about it." Can modify nouns as an adjective: どうしようもない{状況|じょうきょう} (hopeless situation). The contracted form どうしようもねえ is used in rough masculine speech. A similar but slightly milder expression is しかたがない / しょうがない (it can't be helped), which implies acceptance rather than frustration.
